title: Nuclear Power and Secure Energy Transitions
extractedText: Nuclear power today provides about 10% of global electricity and is the second-largest source of low-emissions power after hydropower. In advanced economies, nuclear is the largest single source of low-emissions electricity, but its fleet is ageing and new construction has stalled. Extending the lifetimes of existing plants is among the cheapest sources of additional low-emissions generation available to most countries. Without further lifetime extensions and new construction, nuclear output in advanced economies could fall by two-thirds by 2040, putting additional pressure on wind, solar, and storage to fill the gap. Achieving net-zero pledges would require global nuclear capacity to roughly double between 2020 and 2050, with construction timelines and financing identified as the principal constraints.
